chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
To Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri in the mosque: 'Woe to you, O Abbad! Beware of al-riya' (showing-off), for whoever works for other than Allah, Allah will entrust him to the one he worked for.'

key_terms.الرِّيَاء: Showing-off; performing deeds to be seen and praised by people rather than for Allah alone.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِد: The mosque; the setting for this specific advice, highlighting that even in places of worship, sincerity can be compromised.
key_terms.وَكَلَهُ اللَّهُ: Allah will entrust him/leave him to; a phrase indicating that Allah delegates the reward or consequence to the entity the person was actually serving.

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of showing off (riya') in Islamic worship according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns Abbad ibn Kathir against *riya'* (showing-off), defining it as performing deeds for an audience other than Allah. The theological implication is divine abandonment: if one seeks the pleasure of creation, Allah delegates the reward to that created being, effectively nullating the spiritual value for the Hereafter. This concept is central to Shia ethics, distinguishing between the purity of intention (*ikhlas*) and the corruption of status-seeking.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said to Abd Bin Kaseer Al-Basry in the Masjid: ‘Woe be unto you Abbad! Beware of the showing-off, for it is from the deeds (done) for other than Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Allocate him to the one he worked for’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said to ‘Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri in the Mosque, ‘Woe upon you, O ‘Abbad, you must never show off; whoever works for someone other than Allah, He will assign him to that for which he has worked.’”
